claims.text: Adding 1–2 vol% nanoscale Y2O3 to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will enhance its elevated-temperature mechanical properties.
The Y2O3-containing alloy can be produced from pre-alloyed CoCrFeMnNi powder by hot isostatic pressing at approximately 1100°C.
A subsequent heat treatment at 800–900°C for 10–20 hours will produce the intended oxide-dispersed state.
The proposed processing route will create a uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion.
The dispersed Y2O3 particles will be located in both grain interiors and at grain boundaries.
Nanoscale Y2O3 particles in grain interiors will obstruct dislocation motion.
The nano-oxides will pin dislocations through the Orowan mechanism.
Y2O3 particles at grain boundaries will impede grain-boundary sliding.
Dislocation pinning and suppression of grain-boundary sliding will reduce the high-temperature creep rate.
Dislocation pinning and suppression of grain-boundary sliding will improve elevated-temperature yield strength.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will have at least 20% higher yield strength than CoCrFeMnNi without Y2O3.
The Y2O3-dispersed alloy will have better creep resistance than CoCrFeMnNi without Y2O3.
The predicted strength and creep benefits will hold from 700°C to 900°C.
The specified temperature window and performance enhancement are relevant to turbine-engine and other high-temperature structural applications.
Processing variations and the long-term stability of the oxide dispersion may affect the magnitude of the improvement.
